titleStmt.title: Internally Generated Reactivation of Single Neurons in Human Hippocampus During Free Recall

Mukamel
Harel
Malach

publicationStmt.p: Tag layer of the DHSS Meta-Tagging Project. The article text is reproduced from the staged copy named in sourceDesc and is not altered; the tags are held separately in standOff so that overlapping and nested spans are preserved.

bibl.title: Internally Generated Reactivation of Single Neurons in Human Hippocampus During Free Recall

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: single neurons in human hippocampus and entorhinal cortex, recorded while patients view cinematic episodes and again while they freely recall them
span.quote: we report the activity of single neurons in the human hippocampus and surrounding areas when subjects first view cinematic episodes consisting of audiovisual sequences and again later when they freely recall these episodes

span.label: how MTL neurons respond to episodes presented as film clips, and what they do later when those episodes spontaneously come to mind with no external stimulus present
span.quote: we set out to examine how neurons in the MTL respond to cinematic sequences depicting specific episodes, and, later, when these episodes spontaneously come to mind in the absence of external stimuli, in a free-recall situation that can be reported by individual subjects

span.label: shows that the same single neurons that fired during viewing fire again seconds before the verbal report of free recall, giving spontaneous human recollection a single-neuron correlate
span.quote: Verbal reports of memories of these specific episodes at the time of free recall were preceded by selective reactivation of the same hippocampal and entorhinal cortex neurons.

span.label: existence
span.quote: Verbal reports of memories of these specific episodes at the time of free recall were preceded by selective reactivation of the same hippocampal and entorhinal cortex neurons.

span.label: single-neuron reactivation during free recall
span.quote: The same neurons showed an increased firing rate again with free conscious recall, before the verbal report, when the sequence of physical sensory stimuli was absent and no external cues were provided.

span.label: electrophysiology
span.quote: We recorded from a total of 857 units (441 single units and 416 multi units)

span.label: mechanisms
span.quote: We suggest that this reactivation is an internally generated neuronal correlate for the subjective experience of spontaneous emergence of human recollection.

span.label: temporal precedence carries the causal weight: the neurons rise above baseline about 1500 ms before the verbal report, so the report cannot be what drives the firing
span.quote: The unit’s firing rate rose to more than 3 SD above baseline ( 15 ) about 1500 ms before onset of the verbal report of recall, peaked about 100 ms before verbal report onset, but returned to baseline only after 10 s or more

span.label: the confound is ruled out by signature mismatch rather than by exclusion: epileptic activity is synchronous across neighbouring cells, whereas the observed responses are sparse and isolated among non-responsive neighbours
span.quote: Epileptic activity is characterized by highly correlated activity in large groups of neighboring neurons. The neuronal responses reported here were extremely sparse and seen selectively in individual neurons out of dozens of nonresponsive neurons that were recorded in their immediate vicinity.

span.label: an anatomical dissociation inside the same experiment serves as the control condition: medial frontal units are selective during viewing but lose that selectivity at recall
span.quote: These frontal units exhibited a significant selective increase in firing rate during viewing, but not during recall

span.label: sparseness plus the size of the untested stimulus space is used to infer, without testing, that each neuron must also respond to many episodes never presented
span.quote: it is clear, even by a simple statistical reasoning, that these neurons must display selective responses to multiple other clips that have not been presented, as only a minute fraction of the vast set of possible episodes was tested in our study

span.label: the recall signal is claimed to be readable on one trial rather than only after averaging, which is what lets a single spontaneous recall event be treated as an observation
span.quote: with a robust elevation of firing rate for several seconds that could be detected during a single recall trial

span.label: the recall alignment is to the onset of the patient's own verbal report, so the experiment's time zero is supplied by the subject rather than by the experimenter
span.quote: Traces were aligned on the onset time of the verbal report of recall (zero time, vertical dashed line).

span.label: Findings come from epilepsy patients, so pathology cannot be ruled out with certainty.
span.quote: Although these results should be viewed with caution, such interpretation is unlikely for various reasons.

span.label: Only a tiny fraction of possible episodes was tested, so the apparent selectivity of the neurons is an artefact of the limited stimulus set.
span.quote: The responses to episodes observed here were often remarkably selective and relatively sparse; yet it is clear, even by a simple statistical reasoning, that these neurons must display selective responses to multiple other clips that have not been presented, as only a minute fraction of the vast set of possible episodes was tested in our study

span.label: Which feature of a clip a cell actually responds to cannot be determined.
span.quote: It is also important to exercise caution in claims as to what exact aspect of the clips the cell responded to.

span.label: Regions that might carry top-down recall signals were not sampled.
span.quote: However, it is possible that top-down early recall signals do originate in other frontal or temporal lobe regions not sampled in this study

span.label: Whether the multiple clips a neuron responds to share an abstract association is unresolved.
span.quote: Whether multiple clips to which a neuron responds may be related by some abstract association rule is not clear at present.

span.label: which brain regions were sampled was decided by clinical need, not by the hypothesis — the coverage of the study is a by-product of surgical planning
span.quote: For each patient, the placement of the depth electrodes was determined exclusively by clinical criteria

span.label: the origin of the recall signal may lie in regions the electrodes never reached
span.quote: it is possible that top-down early recall signals do originate in other frontal or temporal lobe regions not sampled in this study

span.label: the subjects all have intractable epilepsy, so a pathology explanation cannot be excluded outright, only argued against
span.quote: Although these results should be viewed with caution, such interpretation is unlikely for various reasons.

span.label: what feature of a clip a cell is actually responding to is undetermined
span.quote: It is also important to exercise caution in claims as to what exact aspect of the clips the cell responded to.

span.label: whether the several clips one neuron responds to share any abstract rule is left open
span.quote: Whether multiple clips to which a neuron responds may be related by some abstract association rule is not clear at present.

span.label: the inhibitory half of the effect could not be resolved in single cells because baseline firing is too low to see a decrease
span.quote: We also noted reactivation of inhibitory responses, but because of the low baseline firing rate, these inhibitory responses were evident only at the population level

span.label: the place-cell response profile — sparse firing from a very low baseline, sharply selective for one condition — imported as the expected shape of a human episode-selective response
span.quote: The sparse neuronal responses arising from a very low baseline to robust firing during a specific episode are reminiscent of the responses of hippocampal place cells in rodents ( 26 ), in which a cell responds whenever the animal is in a particular place in the environment.

span.label: the claim that navigational machinery was conserved and repurposed, used to license reading a spatial-memory literature as a memory literature
span.quote: The hippocampal and entorhinal machinery used in spatial navigation in rodents may have been preserved in humans but put to a more elaborate and abstract use

span.label: response — sustained: elevated firing through most of the clip, up to 12 s
span.quote: Of the responsive units, 46 (9.7%) showed a sustained response to at least one clip, i.e., a significant elevation of firing rate through most of the clip duration (although not necessarily at a fixed level) ( 15 )

span.label: response — transient: elevation only during particular segments of a clip
span.quote: transient ( 15 ) neuronal responses to other clips, i.e., consistent elevation of firing rate above baseline only during particular segments of the clip

span.label: response — the brief 300–600 ms MTL response of the prior stationary-stimulus literature, the sense this paper departs from
span.quote: These responses have been demonstrated for stationary stimuli and are usually brief, often lasting between 300 and 600 ms following stimulus onset, and rarely persist beyond 1 to 2 s

span.label: episode — the general cognitive object: multimodal representations linked in temporal succession
span.quote: we encounter complex stimuli constituting episodes, series of variant multimodal representations linked in temporal succession

span.label: episode — the experimental stimulus, i.e. what a single 5-to-10-s clip depicts
span.quote: Each clip depicted an “episode” featuring famous people, characters, or animals engaged in activity, or landmarks described from various views

span.label: episode — a sub-part contained within one clip, the grain a transient response may be picking out
span.quote: possibly reflecting the preference of the cell to a specific feature of the clip or to an episode within the clip

span.label: unit — single unit (one isolated neuron) versus multi unit (unresolved cluster); both are counted together as units throughout
span.quote: We recorded from a total of 857 units (441 single units and 416 multi units)

span.label: responsive — defined by consistency across all trials of a clip, not by response size
span.quote: A unit was considered responsive to a specific clip if it showed a consistent elevated pattern of firing in all trials of that clip.

span.label: recall — the internal event, versus the verbal report that makes it observable; the paper keeps these apart and measures the lag between them
span.quote: they were asked to freely recall the clips they had seen and to verbally report immediately when a specific clip “came to mind”

span.label: extends → rodent studies of internally generated hippocampal replay during sleep, rest and waking (refs 27-33)
span.quote: Our results from conscious human patients, who can spontaneously declare their memories, now directly link free recall and neuronal replay in hippocampus and entorhinal cortex.

span.label: extends → prior reports of selective single-unit activation during mental imagery of stationary stimuli (ref 25)
span.quote: However, unlike the situation in our study, subjects were cued by an external, content-specific, sensory stimulus.

span.label: extends → rodent work on internally generated hippocampal replay (refs 27–33), which could not be tied to recall because the animal cannot declare a memory
span.quote: However, the relation of such replay in rodents to recall of past navigation events has been merely conjectural.

span.label: extends → neuroimaging studies of reinstatement at recall (refs 21–24), whose resolution could not reach single neurons
span.quote: Several neuroimaging studies show that brain activity present during the learning of information, as indirectly measured by the BOLD signal, is reinstated during cued or free recall ( 21 – 24 ), although spatiotemporal limits of fMRI restrict the possible conclusions.

span.label: contradicts → the prior single-unit picture of MTL responses as brief, 300–600 ms events that rarely outlast 1 to 2 s
span.quote: Responses observed were as long as 12 s and were usually attenuated only by the onset of the next clip.

span.label: extends → prior single-unit imagery work (ref 25), which used an external content-specific cue
span.quote: However, unlike the situation in our study, subjects were cued by an external, content-specific, sensory stimulus.

span.label: builds-on → the established finding that human MTL neurons respond selectively to complex stimuli, categories and individual persons or landmarks (refs 5–11)
span.quote: Human MTL neurons respond in a highly specific manner to complex stimulus features ( 5 ), to complex stimulus categories ( 5 , 6 ), to individual persons or landmarks ( 7 – 9 ), and to previously seen and novel stimuli ( 5 , 10 , 11 ).

span.label: free recall —contrasted-with→ recognition memory
span.quote: Whereas the neuronal basis of recognition memory can be probed experimentally in human and nonhuman primates, the study of free recall requires that the mind declare the occurrence of a recalled memory (an event intrinsic to the organism and invisible to an observer).

span.label: replay —renamed-across-fields→ reactivation
span.quote: Our results from conscious human patients, who can spontaneously declare their memories, now directly link free recall and neuronal replay in hippocampus and entorhinal cortex.

span.label: reinstated —renamed-across-fields→ reactivation
span.quote: Several neuroimaging studies show that brain activity present during the learning of information, as indirectly measured by the BOLD signal, is reinstated during cued or free recall ( 21 – 24 ), although spatiotemporal limits of fMRI restrict the possible conclusions.

span.label: sustained response —distinct-from→ transient
span.quote: Overall, responsive units significantly responded in a sustained or transient manner to an average of 17.7% ± 0.7 SEM of the clips presented

span.label: reactivation —operationalised-as→ FR ratio
span.quote: We calculated the average ratio of firing rate during viewing of clips to baseline firing rate (FR ratio) ( 15 ), for all responsive entorhinal cortex and hippocampal units

span.label: reactivation —is-a→ neuronal correlate
span.quote: We suggest that this reactivation is an internally generated neuronal correlate for the subjective experience of spontaneous emergence of human recollection.

span.label: episode —contrasted-with→ stationary stimuli
span.quote: However, the human experience is seldom that of stationary stimuli; rather, we live and operate in a constantly changing environment.

span.label: mental imagery —contrasted-with→ free recall
span.quote: Selective increases in single-unit activation during mental imagery of stationary stimuli have been reported ( 25 ). However, unlike the situation in our study, subjects were cued by an external, content-specific, sensory stimulus.

span.label: hippocampus —part-of→ medial temporal lobe
span.quote: The human hippocampus and its associated structures in the medial temporal lobe (MTL) transform present experience into future conscious recollections

span.label: baseline firing rate —operationalised-as→ depth electrodes
span.quote: 5-s blank periods were presented occasionally within groups of successive clips and were used to calculate the baseline firing rate, denoted by a gray horizontal line.

span.label: verbal report —operationalised-as→ free recall
span.quote: they were asked to freely recall the clips they had seen and to verbally report immediately when a specific clip “came to mind” (free-recall session)

span.label: anterior cingulate —part-of→ medial frontal
span.quote: Same as (A) but for cells from anterior cingulate ( n = 56). Note that, in contrast to hippocampal and entorhinal cortex cells, although these cells exhibited selectivity during viewing (top), this selectivity was not maintained during free recall (bottom).

span.label: statistics
span.quote: There were no differences in proportion of responsive units among the various regions sampled in this study [ P > 0.05, χ 2 ( 5 ) = 7.6] (table S1).

span.label: statistics
span.quote: Each time this clip was shown, the firing rate was elevated to an average of 15.57 Hz, compared with 2.11 and 2.23 Hz during other clips and blank periods, respectively ( P < 10 −9 , two-sample t test).

span.label: statistics
span.quote: During recall of the preferred clip (red), the averaged firing rate of the neurons increased significantly above baseline in the 3 s before onset of verbal report of recall and remained significantly above baseline in the ensuing 2 s ( P < 0.05, Student’s t test)

span.label: statistics
span.quote: Patients spontaneously recalled a mean of 83.2% (±5% SEM) of the clips presented.

span.label: statistics
span.quote: The unit’s firing rate rose to more than 3 SD above baseline ( 15 ) about 1500 ms before onset of the verbal report of recall, peaked about 100 ms before verbal report onset, but returned to baseline only after 10 s or more

span.label: statistics
span.quote: Spike raster plot and instantaneous firing rate (spike train convolved with a Gaussian of the full width at half maximum of 1200 ms) are displayed together.

span.label: statistics
span.quote: P < 10 −9 , two-sample t test

span.label: statistics
span.quote: ( P < 0.05, Student’s t test)

span.label: statistics
span.quote: a mean of 83.2% (±5% SEM) of the clips presented

span.label: statistics
span.quote: gray dashed line denotes the average firing rate during the recall session + 3 SD

span.label: statistics
span.quote: the corresponding raster plots (six trials, order of trials is from top to bottom) and post–stimulus time histogram (500-ms bins) are given

span.label: A subset of human medial temporal lobe neurons fired selectively and in a sustained way throughout and after specific video episodes, for durations up to 12 seconds.
span.quote: A subset of these neurons exhibited selective firing, which often persisted throughout and following specific episodes for as long as 12 seconds.

span.label: The same hippocampal and entorhinal neurons reactivated before the patient verbally reported freely recalling the corresponding episode.
span.quote: Verbal reports of memories of these specific episodes at the time of free recall were preceded by selective reactivation of the same hippocampal and entorhinal cortex neurons.

span.label: The reactivation effect held at the population level in hippocampus and entorhinal cortex but was absent in medial frontal units, which were selective during viewing only.
span.quote: This recurrence during free recall of the same selective neuronal responses present during viewing was found in the population of hippocampal and entorhinal units but not in medial frontal units

span.label: In an individual recall trial, firing rose above baseline roughly 1.5 seconds before the verbal report and peaked shortly before speech onset, preceding rather than following the report.
span.quote: The unit’s firing rate rose to more than 3 SD above baseline ( 15 ) about 1500 ms before onset of the verbal report of recall, peaked about 100 ms before verbal report onset, but returned to baseline only after 10 s or more

span.label: Episode-specific reactivation was regionally graded: striking for hippocampal and entorhinal cells with sustained responses, weak in amygdala, and absent in parahippocampal gyrus.
span.quote: This episode-specific reactivation phenomenon was weak in amygdala and absent from parahippocampal gyrus

span.label: Over half of all recorded units responded to at least one clip, with no difference in the proportion of responsive units across the sampled regions.
span.quote: Overall, the majority of recorded neurons, 475 units (54.9%), showed a significant response to one or more of the clips, i.e., consistently increased firing rate in at least one 500-ms segment of clip presentation

span.label: The results are unlikely to be an epilepsy artefact because responses were sparse and only a minority of units came from seizure foci, whose exclusion changed nothing.
span.quote: Furthermore, only 27% of the units were recorded from within the epileptogenic seizure foci.

span.label: 475 of 857 recorded units (54.9%) responded to at least one clip
span.quote: the majority of recorded neurons, 475 units (54.9%), showed a significant response to one or more of the clips, i.e., consistently increased firing rate in at least one 500-ms segment of clip presentation

span.label: sustained responses were almost entirely an MTL phenomenon: 44 of the 46 such cells were in MTL, only 2 in medial frontal lobe
span.quote: Of these 46 cells, 44 were in MTL and only 2 in medial frontal lobe [ P < 0.03, χ 2 ( 1 ) = 5.2]

span.label: responses lasted as long as 12 s and were typically ended only by the onset of the next clip
span.quote: Responses observed were as long as 12 s and were usually attenuated only by the onset of the next clip.

span.label: across the population, firing rose above baseline in the 3 s before the verbal report and stayed elevated for 2 s after it
span.quote: the averaged firing rate of the neurons increased significantly above baseline in the 3 s before onset of verbal report of recall and remained significantly above baseline in the ensuing 2 s

span.label: the effect was present in hippocampal and entorhinal units and absent in medial frontal units
span.quote: This recurrence during free recall of the same selective neuronal responses present during viewing was found in the population of hippocampal and entorhinal units but not in medial frontal units

span.label: reactivation was strongest in cells whose viewing response had been sustained rather than transient
span.quote: but was particularly striking for hippocampal and entorhinal neurons with sustained responses

span.label: within MTL the effect was graded by structure: weak in amygdala, absent in parahippocampal gyrus, most prominent in entorhinal cortex
span.quote: This episode-specific reactivation phenomenon was weak in amygdala and absent from parahippocampal gyrus ( fig. S11 ), but was particularly striking for hippocampal and entorhinal neurons with sustained responses

span.label: the proportion of responsive units did not differ across the sampled regions, so region selectivity appears at recall rather than in raw responsiveness
span.quote: There were no differences in proportion of responsive units among the various regions sampled in this study [ P > 0.05, χ 2 ( 5 ) = 7.6]

span.label: removing the 27% of units recorded inside the seizure focus did not change the result
span.quote: Furthermore, only 27% of the units were recorded from within the epileptogenic seizure foci. No significant difference was detected when these units were excluded from the analysis

span.label: cells stayed at baseline during recall of clips that had not driven them at viewing, so the recall response is clip-specific rather than a general recall-state elevation
span.quote: These neurons remained at baseline firing during recall of clips that did not elicit significant responses during viewing (gray).

span.label: the population firing was already slightly elevated before clip onset, which the authors read as anticipation
span.quote: Note small elevation before clip onset, probably attributable to anticipatory effect.

span.label: patients recalled a mean of 83.2% of the clips they had been shown
span.quote: Patients spontaneously recalled a mean of 83.2% (±5% SEM) of the clips presented.
